correction_scope.rationale: The unchanged core requires a same-scope whole-assertion correction. Although instrumental errors are explicitly corrected, the main v1-v4 result also changes selected observations and analysis. Reclassifying the pair as unchanged scope would erase material qualifiers.

evidence.locator: PDF pp.8 and 11; Sections 3 and 5

evidence.bounded_paraphrase: The revised analysis uses 15223 events: 7235 internal and 7988 external. It explicitly excludes about 5% of preselected events whose earliest hit is isolated in time and space, because noise may bias early arrivals.

evidence.locator: PDF pp.5,16,18-21 and 33 / printed pp.2,13,15-18 and 30
evidence.bounded_paraphrase: The paper attributes the earlier anomaly to instrumental effects and applies optical-fibre delay and oscillator corrections. It also adds a revised event selection and analyses, so the main result is not merely a same-observation scalar replacement.

explicit_dependents.rationale: Both proposed dependents (relative-velocity number and anomaly significance/conclusion) have direct replacements in the revised full source. missing_evidence: A complete atomic support graph for every calibration and statistical uncertainty was not certified. No distinct non-direct dependent eligible under the unchanged core was established.

independent_retention.rationale: The separately grounded geodetic baseline is retained in both versions. It is an unaffected control, not sufficient alternative support for the old velocity excess. Alternate analyses and late-2011 experiments are acknowledged without treating them as old-result support or new 2012 substitution.

evidence.locator: PDF pp.9-10; Section 4
evidence.bounded_paraphrase: The dedicated geodesy campaign, GPS benchmarks and terrestrial traverse support a 731278.0 +/-0.2 m BCT-to-OPERA baseline, assembled from two separately measured path lengths.

evidence.locator: PDF pp.11-12 / printed pp.8-9; Section 4
evidence.bounded_paraphrase: The revised paper retains the same 731278.0 +/-0.2 m baseline and geodesy rationale. This measurement is not inferred from the disputed arrival-time result.

evidence.locator: PDF pp.26,28-33 / printed pp.23,25-30; Sections 7-10
evidence.bounded_paraphrase: An alternative waveform analysis gives delta t 3.5 +/-5.6 statistical +9.4/-9.1 systematic ns; the dedicated late-2011 short-bunch run gives separate TT and RPC results. These support revised compatibility and are not surviving support for the exact old 60.7 ns or 6-sigma excess assertions.

missing_evidence: Raw geodesy data and external cited notes were not checked. No formal exhaustive alternative-support proof or OR semantics is claimed.

scope_adjudication.subject: CNGS muon-neutrino velocity measured by OPERA
scope_adjudication.selection_change: About 5% of preselected events with isolated earliest hits discarded in v4. Same nominal running years do not establish identical selected observation scope.
scope_adjudication.new_short_bunch_experiment: Late October to early November 2011; separate from long-extraction main analysis and not a substitution for it.

decision.reason: Full access succeeds but changed selection/reanalysis violates unchanged correction scope. Directly replaced downstream values independently eliminate the proposed propagation advantage.
decision.permitted_development_use: Scope-change exclusion example; a separately frozen scope-aware paired-document reading task may consider these complete versions. This review does not establish an unresolved full-document inconsistency or algorithmic gain.
